charting.authors: Dorothea L. Floris; José O. A. Filho; Meng-Chuan Lai; et al.
charting.primary_focus: Sex-by-diagnosis differences in intrinsic brain function
charting.primary_goal: Characterise robust and replicable sex differences and sex-by-diagnosis interactions in resting-state brain function in autism
charting.country_region: Multi-site (13 merged sites from ABIDE I and II)
charting.diagnosis_assessment: ADI-R and ADOS-2 scores available as phenotypic variables (per Table 1 footnotes); confirmation procedure not restated in main text

charting.specific_features: PCC-seed intrinsic functional connectivity (iFC), voxel-mirrored homotopic connectivity (VMHC), regional homogeneity (ReHo), degree centrality (DC), fractional ALFF (fALFF); Harvard-Oxford atlas used for anatomical labelling of clusters
charting.feature_extraction_tools: Custom R-fMRI pipeline (slice-timing correction, 24-parameter motion regression, CompCor, detrending, band-pass filtering, FSL FLIRT BBR + ANTs registration); C-PAC credited in author contributions for analyses support; ComBat (python, brentp/combat.py) for site harmonisation
charting.feature_change_direction: Sex-by-diagnosis interaction: reduced VMHC in autistic females vs. increased/typical VMHC pattern in the other three groups, localized to dorsolateral occipital cortex
charting.validation_methodology: Voxel-level GLM (Z>3.1, cluster-level P<0.01, GRF-corrected); robustness checked across alternative preprocessing pipelines; replication tested in two independent cohorts (EU-AIMS LEAP, GENDAAR)
charting.summary_key_findings: In the ABIDE I+II discovery sample (N=1019, 13 sites), main effects of diagnosis and sex were found across PCC-iFC, ReHo and VMHC converging on the default-network midline; a sex-by-diagnosis interaction on VMHC in dorsolateral occipital cortex showed reduced VMHC in autistic females and replicated in the larger of two independent cohorts (EU-AIMS LEAP) but not GENDAAR.
charting.features_associated_disorder: PCC-iFC, ReHo and VMHC group differences along the default-network midline; VMHC sex-by-diagnosis interaction in dorsolateral occipital cortex
charting.future_directions_recommended: A priori harmonisation across discovery and replication datasets; systematic study of sample-related factors affecting replicability.

procedures resulted in a total of 297 par-
ticipants (151 ASD and 146 TD) from 4 different sites (i.e., New York University Langone
Medical Center [NYU], University of Pittsburgh, School of Medicine [PITT], University of
Utah, School of Medicine [USM], and Trinity Centre for Health Sciences [TCD]) in ABIDE.
evidence_spans.claim: Final ABIDE sample: 297 participants (151 ASD, 146 TD) from 4 sites (NYU, PITT, USM, TCD).

evidence_spans.text:
For ABIDE, we considered data from all acquisition sites with at least 10 participants per
group and with both children and adults. After detailed quality control, only cases with accept-
able T1-weighted (T1w) MRI, surface extraction, and head motion in rs-fMRI were included.
evidence_spans.claim: ABIDE sites required at least 10 participants per group and both children and adults; QC required acceptable T1w MRI, surface extraction, and acceptable head motion in rs-fMRI.

evidence_spans.text:
Participants with ASD were diagnosed based on an in-person interview administered by
board-certified mental health professionals using the gold standard diagnostics of the Autism
Diagnostic Observation Schedule (ADOS) [51] and/or Autism Diagnostic Interview-Revised
(ADI-R) [52,53].
evidence_spans.claim: ASD diagnosis was based on an in-person interview using ADOS and/or ADI-R gold-standard diagnostics.

evidence_spans.text:
For the resting-state functional brain scans in ABIDE, we built on data previously made
available by the Preprocessed Connectomes initiative (http://preprocessed-connectomes-
project.org/abide). The preprocessing was performed with C-PAC (https://fcp-indi.github.io)
and included slice time correction, head motion correction, skull stripping, and intensity nor-
malization. The rs-fMRI data were detrended and adjusted for common nuisance effects
related to head motion, white matter, and cerebrospinal fluid signals using CompCor [58], fol-
lowed by band-pass filtering (0.01 to 0.1 Hz).
evidence_spans.claim: ABIDE rs-fMRI was preprocessed via the Preprocessed Connectomes initiative using C-PAC (slice-time correction, motion correction, skull stripping, intensity normalization, CompCor, band-pass filtering).

evidence_spans.text:
Func-
tional connectivity matrices were calculated at a single-participant level based on a widely used
parcellation atlas with 100 cortical regions [61].
evidence_spans.claim: Functional connectivity matrices were computed using a 100-region (Schaefer-Yeo) cortical parcellation atlas.

evidence_spans.text:
After matching, we ended up with 290 participants (145 participants per group)
in ABIDE and 126 (63 participants per group) in HBN, which were used subsequently for the
classification of ASD versus TD in both datasets.
evidence_spans.claim: After propensity-score matching on age, sex and site, 290 ABIDE participants (145 per group) were used for classification.

evidence_spans.text:
Similar to the computation of the pro-
pensity scores, we performed deconfounding prior to our analyses, based on all the available
participants instead of using only the training
evidence_spans.claim: Propensity scores and deconfounding were computed using all available participants rather than training data only.

evidence_spans.text:
In the ABIDE cohort, when we trained and
tested on data with similar distributions (first column), the contiguous scheme reached better
prediction performance than the diverse scheme, with the random scheme lying in between.
This trend remained stable as we increased the number of strata used for training.
evidence_spans.claim: In ABIDE, training and testing on similarly-distributed (contiguous) strata achieved better prediction than diverse strata.

evidence_spans.text:
we can observe a decline in performance in ABIDE as diversity increased in both within
(AUC: r = −0.630, F1 score: r = −0.568) and out-of-distribution (AUC: r = −0.671, F1 score:

evidence_spans.claim: In ABIDE, prediction performance declined as participant diversity increased, both within-distribution (AUC r=-0.630) and out-of-distribution (AUC r=-0.671).

evidence_spans.text:
The Automated Anatomical Labelling (AAL) atlas, with 116 ROIs, is widely
used in ASD diagnosis studies [16, 35, 36, 37] due to its ability to provide precise anatomical lo-
cations essential for identifying structural abnormalities caused by ASD. The Craddock 200 atlas
[38], with 200 ROIs, is based on functional connectivity and is particularly useful for analysing
resting-state fMRI data [39, 9, 36, 37], as it clusters the brain into functionally homogeneous
regions.
Recent studies have leveraged multiple atlases to capture diverse patterns related to ASD.
For instance, Mahler et al. [37] proposed a multi-atlas framework for ASD classification using
resting-state fMRI data, employing three atlases, including AAL and Craddock 200. Similarly,
Deng et al. [9] utilised the AAL, Craddock 200 and Craddock 400 atlases. Their experiment in-
dicates that Craddock 200 can outperform Craddock 400 in fMRI-based ASD diagnosis. Hence,
we selected the Craddock 200 atlas, hereinafter referred to as the CC atlas.
To further enhance the analysis, we leverage the Eickhoff-Zilles (EZ) atlas with 116 ROIs,
which has also been utilised in recent ASD diagnosis studies [40, 41]. Derived from cytoarchi-
tectonic mapping, the EZ atlas combines anatomical and functional data, offering a nuanced view
that bridges structural and functional aspects of brain regions
evidence_spans.claim: Three atlases were used: AAL (116 ROIs), Craddock 200 (CC), and Eickhoff-Zilles (EZ).

curacy score of 75.20%, which is a boost of 4.4 percentage points over the best prior work [20]

assessments.support: Raw (1,112) and post-QC (1,035: 505 ASD, 530 TC) Ns, plus NYU subset (182->175) and demographic feature availability, are explicitly reported.
CPAC pipeline (one of four Preprocessed Connectomes Project pipelines) and three named atlases (AAL, CC200, EZ) are explicitly reported.
ASD vs TC labels are taken directly from the ABIDE I release; the diagnostic-instrument source is not independently restated in the main text.

Two leakage-relevant practices: (1) F-score feature selection is described as computed 'for all features in the dataset' rather than confined to training folds; (2) the 'proposed subset' (N=645, accuracy 88.71%) is defined by a pretrained selector model's own correct classifications on the whole dataset, so performance on that subset is tautologically inflated by construction rather than reflecting genuine held-out generalisation.

risk_of_bias.summary: Transparent, code-released, multi-atlas predictive study on ABIDE I with reported 10-fold CV and SOTA whole-dataset accuracy (75.20%), but the 'proposed subset' evaluation (88.71% accuracy) is constructed by selecting samples the classifier itself got right, and F-score feature selection is described as using the whole dataset rather than training folds only — both raise PROBAST Analysis-domain leakage concerns.

charting.title: MADE-for-ASD: A multi-atlas deep ensemble network for diagnosing Autism Spectrum Disorder
charting.authors: Xuehan Liu; Md Rakibul Hasan; et al.
charting.primary_goal: Diagnose ASD vs typical controls from ABIDE I rs-fMRI functional connectivity plus demographic data using a weighted deep ensemble network
charting.data_types: resting-state fMRI, demographic data (age, sex, handedness, FIQ)
charting.dataset_openly_available: Code and evaluations publicly available at https://github.com/hasan-rakibul/MADE-for-ASD
charting.specific_features: Functional connectivity matrices from AAL (116 ROIs), Craddock 200 (CC), and Eickhoff-Zilles (EZ) atlases; top features selected via F-score
charting.top_features_identified: Top 10 ROIs via F-score, e.g. precuneus and anterior cingulate/ventromedial prefrontal cortex
charting.model_category: Deep ensemble (stacked sparse denoising autoencoder + MLP, weighted voting)
charting.validation_methodology: 10-fold cross-validation; evaluated on whole ABIDE I CPAC dataset, a data-selector-defined 'proposed subset', and the NYU site subset
charting.key_performance_results: Whole dataset (N=1035): 75.20% accuracy, 82.90% sensitivity, 69.70% specificity. Proposed subset (N=645): 88.71% accuracy. NYU subset (N=175): 96.40% accuracy, 91.00% sensitivity, 99.50% specificity.
charting.summary_key_findings: MADE-for-ASD achieves 75.20% accuracy on the whole ABIDE I CPAC dataset (N=1035), a 4.4-percentage-point improvement over prior SOTA on the same data, with higher accuracy (88.71%, 96.40%) on a self-selected 'proposed subset' and the NYU site subset respectively; demographic information and multi-atlas fusion are reported to improve performance.
charting.future_directions_recommended: Improve interpretation of fMRI-derived features relative to autism symptoms; extend interpretability and clinical correlation of deep learning outputs.
charting.reviewer_notes: The 'proposed subset' (645/1035, 88.71% accuracy) is defined as samples a pretrained selector model itself classified correctly — this is a circularity/leakage concern when reporting that subset's accuracy as a performance result.

charting.title: Promises, Pitfalls, and Basic Guidelines for Applying Machine Learning Classifiers to Psychiatric Imaging Data, with Autism as an Example
charting.primary_focus: Diagnosis / methodological tutorial on ML classification pitfalls
charting.primary_goal: Demonstrate and compare ML classification pipelines for ASD vs TD using ABIDE RS-fMRI data, while teaching methodological pitfalls (peeking/double-dipping, site effects)
charting.dataset_openly_available: MATLAB code for all pipelines publicly available (ETH website)
charting.specific_features: 200x200 Craddock-atlas ROI-to-ROI Pearson correlation matrix (19,900 features)
charting.feature_extraction_tools: SPM12 (realignment, DARTEL normalization, smoothing, band-pass filter 0.01-0.05Hz, motion scrubbing)
charting.importance_method: Mean-difference threshold feature selection (t-value threshold), with nested CV for threshold tuning
charting.specific_algorithms: Logistic regression, lasso-regularized logistic regression, linear SVM, probabilistic neural network, linear discriminant analysis, Gaussian naive Bayes
charting.validation_methodology: Nested 10x10-fold cross-validation (outer loop for performance, inner loop for feature-selection/tuning-parameter selection); explicit avoidance of double-dipping via train-only feature selection and standardization
charting.key_performance_results: LR 58%, LassoLR 58%, SVM 63% (best out-of-the-box), PNN 58%, LDA 57%, GNB 61% accuracy; SVM accuracy increased to 68% after per-site (train-only) z-standardization; all classifiers significantly better than chance (p<0.001).
charting.summary_key_findings: Out-of-the-box ML classifiers applied correctly (nested CV) to ABIDE rs-fMRI connectivity achieve about 60-70% accuracy (best: SVM 63%, improving to 68% with site standardization); incorrect feature selection on the full dataset ('peeking'/double-dipping) can spuriously inflate accuracy to 91% in a null simulation, illustrating a major pitfall in the field.
charting.future_directions_recommended: Leave-one-site-out cross-validation and further site-effect correction beyond linear z-transformation; stable feature selection methods for biomarker interpretation.
charting.reviewer_notes: A methods/tutorial paper that nonetheless performs an original classification analysis on real ABIDE data; valuable as a positive worked example of leakage-avoidance practice for the review's CL5 checklist item.

among 1112 datasets from the ABIDE datasets

evidence_spans.text:
We excluded
datasets from the social brain Lab BCN NIC UMC Groningen
and Netherlands Institute for Neurosciences due to the missing
information of a full-scale intelligence quotient (IQ) for many
subjects. After preprocessing, we found that a large part of the
cerebellum was missing in the imaging dataset of Carnegie
Mellon University, and all datasets from Carnegie Mellon
University were excluded. To control for potential confounding
eﬀects of IQ in our analysis, we decided to exclude ﬁve datasets
that included some subjects with IQ lower than 70. Finally, we
performed voxel-wise group comparisons with 975 imaging
datasets.
evidence_spans.claim: Sites/datasets were excluded for missing FIQ (Groningen), incomplete cerebellar coverage (Carnegie Mellon), or low IQ (<70, five further datasets), leaving 975 datasets for voxel-wise comparison.

evidence_spans.text:
Datasets were preprocessed with SPM8 (http://www.ﬁl.ion.ucl.
ac.uk/spm/software/spm8/). The ﬁrst step was realignment for
head motion correction. Images were realigned to the ﬁrst
image and a mean echo planar image (EPI) was created during
this step. Subsequently, structural T1 images were coregistered
to their mean EPI data. Registered EPI data of each subject
were normalized to Montreal Neurological Institute (MNI)
template and spatially smoothed with 8 mm of full-width at half-
maximum. Then, in the temporal domain, the linearly increasing
trend due to heat absorption was removed at each voxel, and
the eﬀects of the head motion, white matter, cerebrospinal ﬂuid,
and global signal were regressed out. Lastly, temporal band-pass
ﬁltering was applied (0.01–0.08 Hz).
evidence_spans.claim: Data were preprocessed with SPM8: realignment, coregistration, MNI normalization, 8mm smoothing, detrending, nuisance regression (motion, WM, CSF, global signal), band-pass filtering.

evidence_spans.text:
2-tailed t-test design with two covariates of age
and sex was used to compute the statistical signiﬁcance of the
FCD diﬀerences between the two groups. Statistical signiﬁcance
was based on the false discovery rate corrected P < 0.05 together
with requiring 20 voxels for the minimum continuous voxel
size within a cluster (corrected P < 0.05).

narrative_row.methods: SPM8-preprocessed rs-fMRI; whole-brain voxel-wise functional connectivity density (global, inter-hemispheric/contralateral, intra-hemispheric/ipsilateral) with a 2-tailed t-test (age, sex covariates), FDR-corrected P<0.05, 20-voxel minimum cluster size.
narrative_row.outcomes: Decreased inter- and intra-hemispheric FCD in ASD vs TDC in posterior cingulate cortex, lingual/parahippocampal gyrus, and postcentral gyrus; ADOS-RRB negatively correlated with FCD in these and default-mode-network regions.

narrative_row.relevance_notes: A voxel-wise (non-atlas) associational use of ABIDE I illustrating a common gap in this corpus: multi-site pooling without explicit site-effect statistical handling.
